NRL Team List: Round 27 v Storm
Plenty of changes for the Sharks in their final round clash against the Storm on Saturday night.
Riley Jones #567 is set to make his Cronulla club debut, while Michael Gabrael #568 and Riley Pollard #569 have been named to make their NRL debuts.
Jones is a 24-year-old from Gosford, who debuted for the Knights at hooker in 2023 before making the switch to the Sharks, where he's dominated for the Jets this season. He's a versatile centre who has played everywhere in the backline and at hooker.
His centre partner, Gabrael, is a Wentworthville product with lightning speed who came to Cronulla in 2023. The 21-year-old was the equal 3rd top try scorer in NSW Cup last year and has 27 tries and 10 assists from his 32 games for Newtown.
Pollard is another Jet setting the Cup alight, and the young halfback from Penrith will now take the next step. The 20-year-old graduated from Jersey Flegg last year and has now played 33 games for Newtown, scoring 11 tries, setting up 21 assists and kicking 51 goals at 75%.
Pollard will partner Niwhai Puru in the halves, with Hohepa Puru at 9 and the ever-reliable Will Kennedy at the back making up the spine.
Outside back Mawene Hiroti succumbed to a rib injury in the club's recent loss to the Eels and will now miss the Melbourne match.
Nicho Hynes, Blayke Brailey, Teig Wilton and KL Iro will all be rested with the Sharks locked into either 5th or 6th on the ladder.
Cronulla cult hero Toby Rudolf has been named on the bench to play his first NRL game since injuring his knee in the club's round 15 win over the Warriors in Auckland.
The Sharks will celebrate Old Boys Round and the 10-year anniversary of the 2016 premiership on Saturday against the Storm.

On old boys’ day around 180 Great White Sharks will be in attendance, including the majority of the 2016 Premiership winning squad, when the Sharks play the Storm in the final game of the home and away season at Ocean Protect Stadium on Saturday night .
Currently fifth, despite winning just one of their past four games, the Sharks will host a Storm side which has found form of late but sit in 11th position with no chance of taking part in the NRL Finals for just the fourth time in Club history.
However, while entrenched in the top eight and set to host a finals match next week, coach Craig Fitzgibbon was hoping to see his team gain some confidence against a difficult opponent, while building momentum for the games to come.
“It’s been an up and down period over the last month, but we’re playing Melbourne who are playing really well, and we are excited about this opportunity.
“It’s been a real challenge for us to not think ahead and about playing finals and we’ve taken some lessons from the last few weeks, but we want to play like Sharks, not play not to lose.
“It’s old boys day, the 10-year reunion, we’ve got three debutants, so there’s plenty of excitement around the group.”
With their position in the top eight assured, Fitzgibbon has decided to rest a handful of regulars, while giving Michael Gabrael, Riley Jones and Riley Pollard, the opportunity to show what they can produce at the elite level.
“They’ve all been close (to playing NRL) and now all three get a chance at the one time,” Fitzgibbon said.
Half back Pollard, at 21 years of age and while still Jersey Flegg eligible, has impressed playing for the Jets in the NSW Cup, centre Michael Gabrael has genuine speed and an ability to find the try line, while utility Riley Jones, with one NRL game to his name at the Knights as a hooker, has made a success of a permanent move into the backline while playing for Newtown in 2026.
The trio come into the side for the likes of Nicho Hynes, Braydon Trindall and KL Iro, Mawene Hiroti is unavailable with a rib problem, Tom Hazelton is serving a one match suspension, while hooker and co-captain Blayke Brailey and backrower Teig Wilton will also sit out Saturday's game.
In looking into the history of games played between the two teams, on the 50 occasions they have met, the Sharks have won 18 and the Storm 32, including the two most recent matches and three of the past four games.
At Ocean Protect Stadium the record favours the Sharks, with 10 wins from 18 games against Melbourne, including the last four. The Cronulla team also have a 7-2 record at their home ground this season.
The Sharks and Storm haven’t played in 2026, their last meeting coming in the 2025 Preliminary Final, with Melbourne progressing to play the Broncos in the Grand Final following a 22-14 victory at AAMI Park.
Obviously the most memorable clash between the two took place in 2016 in the competition decider, a match which saw the Sharks claim their maiden premiership title with a 14-12 victory.
In diving deeper into the stats, the Sharks are scoring the second most points per game (28.3) of any team in the NRL this year, trailing only the Warriors (30.3). They have never finished a season with a higher average.

Although the Storm may be missing the finals for the first time in 16 years, the emergence of players like Siulagi Tuimalatu-Brown are a sign of the green shoots of success to come into the future.
A standout last week in their 46-20 Round 26 win over the Broncos, the Victorian Altona Roosters product scored three tries – including one length-of-the-field intercept – ran 170 run metres and had three tackle breaks.
While devastating, the club’s crippling injury toll this year, including to representative winger Xavier Coates who took no part in the season, has given players like “Lagi” the opportunity to gain valuable experience in the NRL.
Named on the wing for his 13th game as the Storm draw the curtain on their season on Saturday against Cronulla, Tuimalatu-Brown said he was grateful for what he had learnt this year.

NRL Gameday Guide: Round 27 v Storm
The Cronulla-Sutherland Sharks are celebrating Old Boys Round and the 10-year anniversary of the 2016 premiership this Saturday when the 2026 team take on the Melbourne Storm.
The 5th-placed Sharks return to Ocean Protect Stadium for their last home game of the regular season, hoping to gain momentum before finals.
The Storm will be out to spoil the party after missing out on the NRL's top 8 for the first time since 2010.
There'll be plenty of action for fans on and off the field with Cronulla calling for fans to get behind them, and the old boys will be in the house to spur them on.
Here's all you need to know in our round 27 game day guide!
Key Timings: Saturday, September 5th 5.35pm – Gates Open 5.45pm – SCORE Sharks v SCORE Dragons Equal Access Exhibition Game 7.00pm - Cronulla Old Boys lap of honour 7.35pm – NRL Kick-Off: Sharks v Storm 8.25pm - Half-Time Tribute to 2016 Sharks 9.20pm – NRL Full-Time (approx.)

Old Boys Day and 2016 Premiers Celebration Catch the 2016 Sharks returning to Ocean Protect Stadium and celebrate the 10-year anniversary of the historic premiership with them.
Paul Gallen and his team of champions will have their reunion earlier in the day before joining a host of other Cronulla old boys at the game, where they'll do a lap of honour at 7pm. Fans are encouraged to arrive early to cheer them on.
Then a special tribute to the 2016 team at half-time, with the premiership-winning side presented to the crowd.
Make sure you stick around after the game as we farewell our departing players with a special lap of honour.
And check out the new mural of Andrew Fifita's 2016 match-winning try, which is painted on the southern side of the ET Grandstand, Thanks to Telstra celebrating 25 years as the NRL's major sponsor.

Simply stay posted to the Ticketek page to see if any tickets are back on the market. Members unable to attend can put their seats up for resale via the Sharks Membership portal .

Cronulla Sharks host Melbourne Storm in Round 27 of the 2026 NRL season at Ocean Protect Stadium on Saturday, 5th September at 7:35 PM AEST. Read on for our full match preview, betting tips, and best odds.
The fifth-placed Sharks have rested a host of players from this relatively inconsequential clash with the 11th-placed Storm.
FORM: The wheels have fallen off for the Sharks, losing three of their last four – including an inexplicable 38-18 defeat to the Eels last Sunday.
The Storm have bookended a 22-14 loss to the Panthers with high-scoring wins over the Sea Eagles (42-20) and Broncos (46-20) in their past three.
INS AND OUTS: Debutant Michael Gabrael and one-gamer Riley Jones are the Sharks’ centres with Mawene Hiroti and KL Iro out. Nicho Hynes has also been rested, so Niwhai Puru and Riley Pollard are in the halves. Hohepa Puru and Billy Burns replace rested duo Blayke Brailey and Teig Wilton.
The Storm are unchanged.
KEY MATCH-UP: Addin Fonua-Blake needs to find some mongrel ahead of the finals. A clash with fellow NSW rep Stefano Utoikamanu provides that opportunity.
HISTORY: The Storm have won nine of their last 12 against the Sharks, winning 30-6 during the regular season and 22-14 in the preliminary final last season – both at AAMI Park – after the Sharks had won 31-26 at home earlier in the year.
KEY STAT: The Sharks are 7-2 at Ocean Protect Stadium in 2026. The Storm are 4-8 away from Melbourne.
VERDICT: The Sharks’ performance last week was borderline disgraceful when they were still in the Top 4 hunt and the only thing saving from a likely immediate finals exit is a probable week one date with the Cowboys.
Opting to rest Hynes, Brailey and their centres, the Sharks have shown little interest in winning this game. Although they’ll finish with a losing record for the first time since 2002, the Storm have shown character all season – particularly over the past couple of months in the face of injuries.
With the big three on deck and a couple of farewells providing motivation, expect the Storm to win easily.

The NRL regular season wraps up this weekend – and there’s less at stake than your average Round 27 with the Top 8 already confirmed.
But the minor premiership is still up for grabs and there’s jostling for other positions, equating to home finals in week one, to unfold.
The final round begins with a dead rubber at Accor Stadium as two of 2025’s top-four outfits wrap up their campaigns.
FORM: The Bulldogs have lost three of their last four, with their finals hopes extinguished thanks to a 24-10 loss to the Panthers last week.
The Broncos have lost 13 of their last 15, following up a comeback win in Canberra with a 46-20 home defeat to the Storm last week.
INS AND OUTS: The Bulldogs are unchanged, though Kurt Mann could be a late inclusion. The Broncos’ only change is on the bench with Blake Mozer replaced by Ben Talty.
KEY MATCH-UP: Payne Haas will be eager to inflict some damage in his last game for the Broncos. Max King and Leo Thompson need to meet Haas and twin tower Xavier Willison head on.
HISTORY: The Broncos have won eight of their last nine against the Bulldogs, including a 32-12 result in Round at Suncorp Stadium.
KEY STAT: The Bulldogs haven’t beaten the Broncos in Sydney since 2019.
VERDICT: While this may be a deflating exercise for the Bulldogs after their finals bid officially ended last week, their form has been strong overall and they showed plenty of backbone against the Panthers.
The Broncos have been gagging for the end of a disastrous title defence for some time and have conceded 30-plus points in five straight games. It’s a road trip this injury-ravaged side doesn’t want to be on.

The Dolphins have won six straight, moving to third spot via an impressive 26-12 defeat of the Roosters at Allianz Stadium.
INS AND OUTS: Beau Fermor is back for the Titans, while Luke Sommerton replaces Oliver Pascoe (concussion). Dolphins winger Selwyn Cobbo is out, which sees Tevita Naufahu come in.
KEY MATCH-UP: Kodi Nikorima has been in hot playmaking form for the Dolphins. Titans No.6 Jayden Campbell will be eager to finish the season with a flourish.

KEY STAT: Phillip Sami and Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow have both scored four tries in six Titans-Dolphins games.

The Titans have been meandering towards the end of the season and showing an increasingly lacklustre attitude towards defending, leaking 30-plus points in their past five games – after only doing so six times in their previous 17 games. They didn’t name winger Selwyn Cobbo , and Kodi Nikorima and Kulikefu Finefeuiaki , while named on Tuesday, will also drop out of this week’s team. Cobbo (ankle), Nikorima (hamstring) and Finefeuiaki (knee) will be given an extra week to get themselves right for the club’s first finals appearance next week. “Selwyn’s had a bit of an ankle injury that has just been pestering him for a little while so it was a good opportunity for us to rest that up,” Woolf said. “Kodi had a tight hamstring through the game the other day that we were worried about.
